claims.kickoff_quote: plus model and effort on every track.
claims.skill_quote: Closest sentence is the agent's own framing, which assigns model/effort selection to *downstream* consumers rather than to the planner: 'are what `gate-plan-review` and `sprint-execution` use to validate or select model/effort; emit them honestly rather than deriving model/effort first and back-filling signals to match.' references/complexity-signals.md line 3 reinforces the same split — 'Planners emit signals; gates and executors consume them.' Greps run: `grep -n -E '\beffort\b|model:|model/effort' agents/planner.md` → only lines 146, 516, 517, none instructing emission; `grep -rn -E 'Model:|Effort:|\*\*Model\*\*|model/effort' references/planning/ agents/planner.md` → only 516/517; `grep -n -iE 'model|effort' skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md` → only line 120, same framing. The PLAN.md frontmatter table (lines 498-510) has no model or effort field.
claims.reasoning: Nothing in the planner or its references tells it to declare a per-track model and effort, yet the downstream consumer expects them: sprint-execution SKILL.md line 39 says 'The plan's Parallel Execution Map header states the orchestrator model and per-track models; honor it.' So the KICKOFF clause is load-bearing and must be kept. There is also mild tension worth flagging to the owner: complexity-signals.md line 3 says planners emit signals only, so the fix may be a contract decision, not just an added sentence.
